analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES Net vs gross confusion; SpaceX buys spectrum ve Telcos; Rightmove no announcement; Classified incoming 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: AI equities sold off after the FT reported OpenAI annualised revenue was about $50bn at end-September versus the widely cited $68-70bn. The gap reflects reporting basis: OpenAI reports closer to net of cloud-partner sales, Anthropic closer to gross.

On a like-for-like view OpenAI's progression was nearer $30bn to $50bn than $40bn to $70bn, still roughly 70% growth but below elevated expectations. Press says OpenAI still targets about $70bn annualised by year-end.
Most exposed names to OpenAI: Microsoft (largest partner/investor), Oracle (compute provider), Nvidia (GPU supplier) and CoreWeave. Secondary exposure: Broadcom, AMD and other capacity-related names.

Oracle and Broadcom credit spreads are flagged as indicators of concern over debt-funded AI capex. Oracle 5-year CDS closed at a record 261bp (up 36% on the month) and Broadcom 5-year CDS printed a record 136bp, as nearly $500bn of 2026 AI-related borrowing is being repriced.

The desk reads the OpenAI episode as an expectations reset, not a growth collapse. Futures stabilized overnight with no further negative revision, and the desk's bottom line is that the underlying demand signal remains strong.
Apples-to-oranges volatility from differing reporting conventions is likely to persist until both labs are public or adopt consistent metrics.

SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide portfolio of low-band 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management, including up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum previously bought from T-Mobile. Price is undisclosed, reports suggest about $8bn, and the deal needs FCC approval.

AT&T, T-Mobile US and Verizon fell roughly 6-7% post-market on the SpaceX spectrum deal. The desk expects selling first, with US names more exposed given the price of mobile, and flags possible weakness in European telcos, especially Deutsche Telekom.

The spectrum could support hybrid satellite and terrestrial service on existing smartphones, but becoming a full national carrier would still require large terrestrial infrastructure, capital and regulatory support. The deal does not immediately replace incumbent US networks.
US tower companies rose on the SpaceX deal. The desk is watching whether Cellnex holds, on the thesis that SpaceX will need a terrestrial network to infill satellite coverage.

Rightmove shares jumped on a Betaville report of takeover speculation (a Gulf-backed trade buyer or REA Group). Betaville called it 'uncooked' and REA management said at its EGM it had moved on from Rightmove.
With no Rightmove statement despite the price move (UK Takeover Panel Rule 2.2), the desk reads the report as low quality with no talks, and expects the stock to fade.

Wise is negotiating a bulk settlement with HMRC after third-party software produced incorrect tax statements for about 4,000 UK investment customers between 2021 and 2025. Shares fell nearly 3% initially, and the issue adds to scrutiny of its anti-money-laundering controls.
Meta launched an integrated commerce stack in conversations with its Muse AI assistant, working with Adyen, PayPal, Shopify and Stripe. The desk notes it as something for Adyen hedge fund bears.

GIR upgraded Palantir to Buy, citing sentiment improvement, a discount on EV/FCF/growth versus software peers, and a wider addressable market via sovereign AI and its Forward Deployed Engineer model. The stock is up 9% YTD.

GIR cut its TietoEVRY FY26 organic revenue growth forecast to about -5% y/y, slightly below company guidance of -3% to -5%, citing Tech Consulting softness and legacy run-offs. Margins are not being trimmed.

GIR retains Buy on Indra ahead of Q3, expecting a solid quarter with Defence revenue near EUR1bn in 1H26 and a EUR11bn-plus backlog. Capital Markets Day is 27 November, with a EUR10bn revenue target before 2030.

The US government temporarily banned Microsoft, Adobe and others from sponsoring workers for permanent residency, and suspended Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini from the Perm programme.
A Lebara-commissioned survey suggests UK mobile customer inertia could cost up to £9bn a year. The desk says to treat the figure cautiously, as it is based on savings from moving to Lebara.

A GS note is constructive on European online classifieds into reporting season. Scout24 is the most positive catalyst, Auto Trader's focus is revenue acceleration into 2H27/FY28, and Rightmove expectations are more cautious. Price targets were lowered for higher bond yields and discount rates.
Meta banned TikTok ads on its platforms in the US (Reuters).

US trading was choppy and top-down, with ETF share of volume around 32%, the highest since June. Headlines on Trump not attacking Iran before the midterms and OpenAI revenue drove flow, with large-cap tech seeing long-only and hedge fund supply.

Semis/AI weakness also reflected underwhelming Samsung and TSM prints versus high expectations, reports of AI players tapping debt markets (ORCL, AVGO, SCPX), and no update on the China optical ban weighing on COHR, LITE and GLW.

About 70% of the S&P finished up with RTY > SPX > NDX. RTY held its 200-day moving average as yields cooled, snapping a 4-day streak of underperformance versus SPX. The GS floor finished -686bps better for sale.

tension_points.bull_case: The gap is a gross versus net reporting difference. OpenAI is still growing about 70%, enterprise more than doubled since July, and it guides to about $70bn by year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: AI names are highly sensitive to the trajectory of two private companies using different conventions, and further clarification could hit Nvidia, Microsoft, Oracle and CoreWeave, with Oracle and Broadcom credit spreads signalling debt-funded capex concern.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further negative revision to OpenAI's revenue figures, or widening Oracle and Broadcom credit spreads.

tension_points.bull_case: The deal does not replace incumbent US networks, since becoming a full carrier needs substantial terrestrial infrastructure, capital and regulatory support, and US towercos rose.
tension_points.bear_case: SpaceX gains a competitive position for direct-to-device coverage, and US carriers sold off 6-7% with European names such as Deutsche Telekom possibly next.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SpaceX attending upcoming spectrum auctions, or the deal failing FCC approval.
